# D11 Lowen Quay (PWL), weeks of 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-24

**Counter and online on-rent days rose sharply for three weeks, then returned to normal. Contract did not clearly change.**

| Channel | Typical level (other weeks) | Nov 10 / 17 / 24 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Counter | ~82–93 | 132 / 131 / 126 | roughly +45–50% |
| Online | ~39–42 | 59 / 61 / 57 | roughly +45% |
| Contract | swings widely (49–143) | 135 / 135 / 129 | within its normal range |

- **Counter and online moved together.** Both stepped up in the week of Nov 10, held for three weeks, and dropped back in the week of Dec 1 (counter 88, online 36).
- **Contract is too noisy to call.** It swings between about 49 and 143 from week to week. The values in this period match several other weeks, such as 143 on Oct 13 and 137 on Dec 15, so I can't say it was affected.

**What the data rules out or can't explain:**
- **Not a West-wide pattern.** D10 Abermoor and D12 Carrick Stowe stayed within their usual ranges during these weeks. D10 was actually at one of its lowest values (243) in the week of Nov 10.
- **Not a pricing change.** No price list changes were recorded anywhere in 2025.
- **No staff notes for D11.** None of the notes for this period mention D11 or explain the increase.
- **Not a data loading gap.** No weekly files were missing for these depots.

**Cause unknown.** The data shows a temporary, local increase in walk-in and online demand at D11, but nothing here explains why. A local event, a short-term project, or a competitor outage are possibilities, but none of these is supported by the data provided. D11 staff or local booking records would be the next place to look.

One smaller point: in the week of Dec 1, right after the increase, all three D11 channels were at or slightly below their usual levels. Contract was especially low at 88. That could be ordinary variation, and the data doesn't explain it either.
